Messages are end to end encrypted and concealed within the routine activity that every Guardian mobile app performs. This prevents an observer from knowing that you are communicating with us at all, let alone what is being said.If you don’t already have the Guardian app, download it (iOS/Android) and go to the menu. Select ‘Secure Messaging’.SecureDropIf you can safely use the tor network without being observed or monitored you can send messages and documents to the Guardian via ourSecureDrop platform.Our guide attheguardian.com/tipslists several ways to contact us securely, and discusses the pros and cons of each.Show moreExplore more on these topicsPoliticsAlcoholHouse of CommonsLondonnewsShareReuse this content

title: Heatwave scorching western US ups risk of hazardous fire conditions | US weather | The Guardian
description: In Oregon and Washington, low humidity and powerful winds have put officials on alert for wildfire spread
Author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
Headline: In Oregon and Washington, low humidity and powerful winds have put officials on alert for wildfire spread
Content: Firefighters burn off vegetation while trying to stop a wildfire called the Bench fire from spreading, in Warm Springs, Oregon, on 25 July.Photograph: Noah Berger/APView image in fullscreenFirefighters burn off vegetation while trying to stop a wildfire called the Bench fire from spreading, in Warm Springs, Oregon, on 25 July.Photograph: Noah Berger/APUS weatherHeatwave scorching western US ups risk of hazardous fire conditionsIn Oregon and Washington, low humidity and powerful winds have put officials on alert for wildfire spreadUwa Ede-OsifoSat 1 Aug 2026 19.39 EDTLast modified on Sat 1 Aug 2026 19.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA heatwave scorching the western US region has elevated the risk of hazardous fire conditions particularly in parts ofOregonand Washington, where low humidity and powerful winds have put officials on alert for wildfire spread.The National Weather Service has forecast blistering temperatures through early next week that could climb from 110F to 120F across the south-west. In the Pacific north-west, highs reaching into the 90s are expected in the days to come.Several western states are dealing with devastating wildfire seasons.In Oregon, about 1.8m acres (730,000 hectares) havereportedlybeen torched, as of July.A rare “particularly dangerous situation” was assigned to a red flag warning in effect for eastern Oregon on Saturday, where weatherofficialshave forecast gusts of wind from 30-40mph.These boots are the safest for US wildland firefighters. Fewer and fewer can afford themRead moreIn Washington, more than 1,000 fires have torn through roughly 425,000 acres, a level of destruction not seen since 2021, according to the state department of natural resources. State officials are also working to contain 12 large fires that cumulatively have set more than 200,000 acres ablaze.The active wildfire year comes as the state is in a drought, owing to insufficient snowpack. The state depends on snowmelt to fill its rivers and reservoirs, but this year, precipitation fell more as rain than as snow,accordingto the Washington department of ecology.The confluence of drought conditions, dangerous heat and strong winds led Washington governor Bob Ferguson to temporarilybanoutdoor burning through the end of September.“Our firefighters are already stretched thin across the state, and with more heat and wind expected this weekend and for the rest of the summer, any new spark on our tinder dry landscapes can lead to another devastating wildfire,” said Dave Upthegrove, the state’s commissioner of public lands, in a news release.Explore more on these topicsUS weatherWest CoastExtreme heatWildfiresOregonWashington stateExtreme weathernewsShareReuse this content

title: Sopranos actor Vincent Pastore, known for playing mobsters and tough guys, dies aged 80 | US news | The Guardian
description: Veteran actor best-known for playing Salvatore ‘Big Pussy’ Bonpensiero, friend of Tony Soprano who becomes FBI informant
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Veteran actor best-known for playing Salvatore ‘Big Pussy’ Bonpensiero, friend of Tony Soprano who becomes FBI informant
Content: Vincent Pastore arrives at the MTV video music awards in Newark, New Jersey, on 26 August 2019.Photograph: Xavier Collin/Image Press Agency/AvalonView image in fullscreenVincent Pastore arrives at the MTV video music awards in Newark, New Jersey, on 26 August 2019.Photograph: Xavier Collin/Image Press Agency/AvalonUS newsSopranos actor Vincent Pastore, known for playing mobsters and tough guys, dies aged 80Veteran actor best-known for playing Salvatore ‘Big Pussy’ Bonpensiero, friend of Tony Soprano who becomes FBI informantAssociated PressSat 1 Aug 2026 18.36 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleVincent Pastore, a veteran actor who played mobsters and tough guys, and was best-known for playing Salvatore “Big Pussy” Bonpensiero onThe Sopranos, has died. He was 80.Bob McGowan, who had managed Pastore since his run on The Sopranos, told the Associated Press that he learned of his death Saturday from another client and actor on the show, Vincent Curatola.He said that Pastore had been found in his home on New York’s City Long Island after not being heard from for a few days.McGowan said he’d been trying to reach Pastore about a possible job.“He was the most loyal client and he always gave to charity,” McGowan said, “and he was the kind of guy who would help anybody, which is rare in my business.”Pastore appeared in movies dating back to the 1980s and had roles in big movies including Goodfellas and Awakenings, both in 1990.He often played gangsters, as with the role he was best-known for: his 30-episode run as Salvatore “Big Pussy” Bonpensiero, the friend of Tony Soprano who becomes an FBI informant in The Sopranos.He was born in the Bronx and grew up in suburban New Rochelle, New York. He enlisted in the navy during the Vietnam war and later attended Pace University, according to his biography on IMDb.He has a daughter, Renee Pastore.Explore more on these topicsUS newsThe SopranosCelebritynewsShareReuse this content

title: California announces minimum wage increase as governor taunts Trump | California | The Guardian
description: Gavin Newsom says new pay floor of $17.40, set to become highest of any US state, will go into effect on 1 January
Author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
Headline: Gavin Newsom says new pay floor of $17.40, set to become highest of any US state, will go into effect on 1 January
Content: A Wendy's restaurant in Fountain Valley, California, on 20 June 2024.Photograph: Jae C Hong/APView image in fullscreenA Wendy's restaurant in Fountain Valley, California, on 20 June 2024.Photograph: Jae C Hong/APCaliforniaCalifornia announces minimum wage increase as governor taunts TrumpGavin Newsom says new pay floor of $17.40, set to become highest of any US state, will go into effect on 1 JanuaryUwa Ede-OsifoSat 1 Aug 2026 16.39 EDTLast modified on Sat 1 Aug 2026 16.40 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCalifornia governorGavin Newsomannounced that the state’s minimum wage will rise to $17.40 next year, a ay floor set to become the highest of any US state.The pay bump will go into effect starting 1 January, Newsomannouncedon Friday. The state’s current minimum rate is $16.90. In a news release, Newsom touted the move as a salve for working families amid high living costs and took a jab at the Trump administration.“For years, Donald Trump and Republicans have blocked efforts to raise the federal minimum wage while handing tax breaks to billionaires and big corporations,” Newsom said.The federal minimum wage was last increased during George W Bush’s presidency, when it rose from $6.55 to $7.25. Opponents of a federal increase fear adverse effects to the labor market such as job losses.“California has chosen a different path – one that rewards work, grows the economy and puts working families first. We believe if you work hard, you deserve a decent paycheck. They think $7.25 an hour is enough. We don’t,” Newsom said.Thirty states in addition to Washington DC have set wage rates above the federal minimum. The state of Washington will trailclosebehind California in 2027 with a minimum wage of $17.13, according to data from the Department of Labor. In New York City and three nearby counties, the minimum wage is $17.Since Newsom took the gubernatorial seat in 2019, the state’s minimum wage has grown from $12, according to his office.Still, for a family of two working adults and two children in California,researchersat the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) estimate each adult must earn $36.38 to cover food, childcare, healthcare, housing and transportation, among other basic necessities.Cost-of-living concerns have been at theforefrontof the upcoming midterm elections. The Trump administration has faced blowback over the protracted war with Iran that has led to a surge in gas prices across the nation. In California, a state that relies on a reduced emission type of gasoline, fuel prices topped $6 per gallon in recent months.Explore more on these topicsCaliforniaMinimum wageGavin NewsomUS politicsWest CoastnewsShareReuse this content

title: There can be no letup. Humiliated Infantino must stand down at Fifa or be removed | Gianni Infantino | The Guardian
description: Uefa’s decisive call for a boycott and declaration of no confidence must be the opening salvos in a concerted push to dethrone the game’s global leader
Author: Nick Ames
Headline: Uefa’s decisive call for a boycott and declaration of no confidence must be the opening salvos in a concerted push to dethrone the game’s global leader
Content: ‘Every day Gianni Infantino remains in power is a fresh stain on an institution whose reputation is on the floor’Photograph: Manu Fernández/APView image in fullscreen‘Every day Gianni Infantino remains in power is a fresh stain on an institution whose reputation is on the floor’Photograph: Manu Fernández/APGianni InfantinoThere can be no letup. Humiliated Infantino must stand down at Fifa or be removedNick AmesUefa’s call for a boycott and declaration of no-confidence must be the opening salvos in push to dethrone game’s global leaderSat 1 Aug 2026 11.00 EDTLast modified on Sat 1 Aug 2026 11.03 EDTShareThere is no time to dance around the subject.Gianni Infantinomust stand down as Fifa president or otherwise be legally removed. No fresh chances can be made available for an official who has demolished trust in football’s integrity and governance, trashing all remaining credibility of the body that oversees the world’s most-cherished sport.Infantino wasforced into a humiliating climbdownon Saturday morning when he accepted the failure of his plan to sell off portions of the World Cup to private investment. He resolved to resume dialogue about football’s growth “in the spirit of shared interest in our game”. But such a naked attempt to save his own skin cannot hold. Every day Infantino remains in power is a fresh stain on an institution whose reputation is on the floor.Gianni Infantino ‘has lost Uefa’s confidence’ after Fifa chief scraps World Cup sell-off planRead moreThe overreach involved in unilaterally launching theFifaForward Enterprise (FFE) scheme – with its vision to place huge influence on football’s future in the palms of venture capitalists – would be enough to bring down most leaders. But Infantino’s rap sheet goes far beyond that. He has routinely made a mockery of Fifa’s own statutes and governance regulations, so nobody should be surprised that patience has finally snapped in corridors of power globally. Fifa’s “football unites the world” slogan has never looked more empty.Article 10.3 of those regulations, which specifically pertains to the presidency, requires the incumbent to ensure “Fifa’s objectives, mission, strategic direction, policies and values are sustainably pursued, protected and implemented, and that a positive image of Fifa is fostered”. It stipulates “promoting friendly and peaceful relations within Fifa”, which is a nonsense given the degree to which federations and senior personnel have distanced themselves from Infantino in recent days.The rules give no green light to the pursuit of multiple private projects that, most recently in lockstep with the current US administration or its tributaries, have been tabled with scant appetite for oversight or explanation.Where to begin?The Folarin Balogun sagatipped many leading figures in football, particularly in Europe, towards the edge. There had already been widespread bafflement and disgust atInfantino’s presentation of the new Fifa peace prizeto Donald Trump in December, with little background given about the process and highly contestable information provided about the US president’s qualifying achievements. Stakeholders were frustrated by a lack of consultation aboutthe introduction of “hydration breaks”, which fundamentally toyed with the fabric of matches at this summer’s World Cup.View image in fullscreenThe saga involving Folarin Balogun after his ban for a red card was suspended tipped many leading figures in football towards the edge.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersThe bizarre expedited bidding process for the 2034 tournament, which resulted in Saudi Arabia’s candidature beingwaved through in December 2024, also brought widespread criticism. This list only covers the past 20 months of controversies inflicted by Infantino, capped on Friday by revelations thatplans for a 64-team World Cup are in full swing.When ascathing statement from Uefa on Saturdaycalled for an end to “secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game”, it was not only referring to the FFE project and its casual sidelining of other decision makers within Fifa.A critical mass has been reached. Uefa took a decisive lead in following more than a year of harsh words with strong, united action inpledging to boycott future Fifa tournamentsif Infantino did not withdraw his plan. It undoubtedly influenced the outcome and the Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, secured an achievement that may define his own reign. But it will mean nothing if Infantino, who is understood to have deployed a major consultancy to smooth relations with federations in recent days, is given the oxygen to dangle fresh promises and turn heads back towards the status quo.View image in fullscreenGianni Infantino’s rap sheet goes far beyond attempting to launch the Fifa Forward Enterprise unilaterally.Photograph: Claudio Thoma/EPAThere is an acknowledgment within Uefa and beyond that the pace must not let up. Senior figures are adamant Infantino must not survive the current scandal. Some insiders feel a crucial next step will be for member associations, the overwhelming majority of whom had formally pledged their support for Infantino’s re-election next March, to recall those letters.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDoing so requires a request to Fifa but could, in sufficient numbers, be a de factovote of no confidencein Infantino. Fifa had lobbied aggressively for those submissions but many FAs would now be red faced if their expression of fealty towards Infantino was more widely publicised.Member associations have a duty not to shrink in staving off existential threats to their sport otherwise they, like Infantino, are doing it an egregious disservice. Backing away now would mean leaving the job half done at best.Uefa have pledged to devise a new method for distributing Fifa’s wealth, delving into its multibillion cash reserves without “selling the family silver”. Behind the scenes it continues to work with other confederations in an effort to find credible candidates for Infantino’s replacement, with a view to running in the election should the Swiss hold on until then. The present crisis can be used to reshape football for the better but only if Infantino is not in situ to impose the final say.The alternative is that Fifa, and by extension the game, continue lurching from one disaster to the next. It is no laughing matter when the public conversation around football centres on one man, his ego and brazen ventures.In December Zvonimir Boban, a former sidekick to Infantino as Fifa’s deputy secretary general,told the Guardian that “the way is lost”after the peace prize award to Trump. Fifa will not find a route back until Infantino plays no further part in its operation.Explore more on these topicsGianni InfantinoFifaWorld Cup 2026World CupFootball politicscommentShareReuse this content

title: Sophie Cunningham says protests over transgender sports stance are not distracting Fever | WNBA | The Guardian
description: Sophie Cunningham said rallies backing her stance on transgender participation in women’s sports have not affected the Fever’s focus as demonstrations continued on the road
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Sophie Cunningham said rallies backing her stance on transgender participation in women’s sports have not affected the Fever’s focus as demonstrations continued on the road
Content: Sophie Cunningham of the Indiana Fever smiles after her team’s win against the Seattle Storm at Climate Pledge Arena on Tuesday.Photograph: Soobum Im/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSophie Cunningham of the Indiana Fever smiles after her team’s win against the Seattle Storm at Climate Pledge Arena on Tuesday.Photograph: Soobum Im/Getty ImagesWNBASophie Cunningham says protests over transgender sports stance are not distracting FeverCunningham says rallies aren’t a distractionSupporters gather outside second straight gameWhite: team wants focus to stay on basketballAgenciesSat 1 Aug 2026 10.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSophie Cunningham says she’s unconcerned that the rallies against transgender participation in women’s sports that have accompanied the Indiana’s Fever’s recent games are a distraction for theWNBAteam.Cunningham made the comments before the Fever’s game Friday night against the Portland Fire. Outside, a group rallied for the second straight game in support of Cunningham and her recent comments about transgender athletes.“I think at the end of the day, I come in and I do my job,” Cunningham said. “I think everyone who knows me personally, they know that I’m full of love. I’m bubbly. I love the people around me. I love basketball. I love inspiring the next generation and doing that in a positive light. And so that doesn’t even cross my mind. Doesn’t cross my teammates’ minds.“And again, I’m here to play basketball, but I’m also here to be me, and I’m not gonna like shadow that or hide or, you know, dim my light just because maybe people don’t agree with that.”Portland’s rally came after a similar rally for Cunningham earlier in the week before the Fever’s game at the Seattle Storm. Both rallies only attracted about two dozen participants and a bevy of onlookers.“I have honestly had nothing to do with them,” Cunningham said. “I think it’s people just practicing their rights of freedom of speech and doing what other fans have been doing since the WNBA has started. And so props to them, props to everyone who is able to be competent and be bold and courageous enough to to speak their truths.”View image in fullscreenPeople rally to support Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham after her comments on transgender athletes in women’s sports before a WNBA game between the Portland Fire and the Indiana Fever on Friday.Photograph: Craig Mitchelldyer/APAnother rally was planned for Sunday in Minneapolis when the Fever play the Minnesota Lynx.In Seattle on Tuesday, two Cunningham supporters sat courtside at Climate Change Arena holding signs. A co-owner of the Storm, Celeste Keaton was later fined an undisclosed amount and suspended for five games by the WNBA for an exchange with the two supporters.The Storm also apologized for the incident, but did not provide details about the exchange, releasing a statement that said: “We remain committed to creating a welcoming and respectful environment for anyone who attends a Storm game.”The Seattle rally promoted statewide ballot initiative, IL26-638, that would bar transgender students from participating in girls’ athletics at Washington schools. It also praised Cunningham, who voiced support for barring transgender athletes from girls’ and women’s sports in recent interviews.“I am here to be a cheerleader for Sophie Cunningham, who has so bravely put her head above the parapet to protect women and girls in our sports and in our locker rooms,” said Amy Souza, who was among those at the Portland rally. “I was an organizer of this event, I was a co-organizer of the Seattle event. I’m also here, standing in solidarity with those teen girls who, unfortunately, were harassed when they were just trying to be fans of the sport, fans of Sophie Cunningham.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Preview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionCunningham was booed by the Moda Center crowd in Portland when she entered the game midway though the first quarter. Many waved small pink, blue and white transgender flags.The Fever downed the Fire 112-98 for their fifth straight win . Cunningham finished with 13 points and Caitlin Clark had her fourth career triple-double with 26 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists.Coach Stephanie White said she was concerned that the controversy was distracting from the team’s play.“You know there is a frustration, of course, because we want to we want to talk about basketball and we want to continue to work on our game and we want to continue to grow as a team.,” White said. “But I also understand this is part of our growth edge as a league, right? It’s part of our growth as a league, and we have to to be able to manage, we have to be able to insulate as much as we can, and then we have to be able to lead with conversation.”Explore more on these topicsWNBAIndiana FeverUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Faster, faster: Iraola in a rush to plug Liverpool gaps before Premier League starts | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: New head coach needs to use the transfer market with defensive cover vital as injuries hamper their US pre-season tour
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: New head coach needs to use the transfer market with defensive cover vital as injuries hamper their US pre-season tour
Content: Liverpool will complete their Chicago pre-season tour with a friendly against Leeds on Sunday.Photograph: Nikki Dyer/Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenLiverpool will complete their Chicago pre-season tour with a friendly against Leeds on Sunday.Photograph: Nikki Dyer/Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesLiverpoolFaster, faster: Iraola in a rush to plug Liverpool gaps before Premier League startsNew head coach needs to use the transfer market with defensive cover vital as injuries hamper US pre-season tourAndy Hunterin ChicagoSat 1 Aug 2026 11.25 EDTLast modified on Sat 1 Aug 2026 12.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google“Faster, faster,” bellowedAndoni Iraolathroughout the open training session Liverpool held in Chicago on Friday. His first pre-season tour as Liverpool head coach ends at the city’s famous Soldier Field Stadium on Sunday, with a friendly against Leeds, and “faster, faster” could apply to all aspects of the club’s preparations for a new Premier League campaign that begins in three weeks’ time.Iraola was in his element as he immersed himself at the centre of every training drill that Liverpool performed at Chicago Fire’s Endeavor Health Performance Center, their base for the past two weeks in the US. “Faster, faster” was the new head coach’s instruction to his players as three teams of seven worked on their pressing games. He also shouted it when they walked over to a different pitch, recently vacated by Robert Lewandowski and his newChicago Fireteammates, to work on offensive and defensive set-piece routines. Sprints were demanded following every rondo.Inter make new approach to Liverpool for Curtis Jones with £30m offer likelyRead moreThere is an urgency to Iraola’s situation atLiverpoolas he works towards his first season in charge, not only to his style of football. Post World-Cup holidays have deprived him of eight first-team players so far, injuries of a further six.It was telling that, after Liverpool’s open training session had ended, many of the fans invited headed to the gym for a look through its glass windows. Jérémy Jacquet, Liverpool’s £60m recruit from Rennes, was inside working on his recovery from a shoulder problem.He was joined by Giovanni Leoni, who is rehabilitating from an anterior cruciate ligament rupture and appears to have doubled in chest size since sustaining the injury on his Liverpool debut last September. Nearby was Joe Gomez, who pulled up with a muscle injury eight minutes into the first friendly of the tour. All central defenders, all out.The concentration of problems in one particular area was a recurring theme under Arne Slot last season and has not eased yet. Two 18-year-olds, Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, have impressed in their absence but Liverpool are looking to loan out the latter next season having been unable to secure a work permit.Among the observers on Friday was Mike Gordon, the president of Liverpool’s owners, Fenway Sports Group, who has returned to a more hands-on role at the club afterthe departure of Michael Edwardsas FSG’s chief executive of football.View image in fullscreenTeenage defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe is likely to be loaned out by Liverppool.Photograph: Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesGordon is expected to be in attendance at Soldier Field on Sunday when Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak should feature for the first time in pre-season. FSG will not be the only ones at Liverpool looking for a return on their combined £241m investment in the pair.“We need a very good version of Florian,” Iraola said this week, when confirming he intends to play the Germany international “in that position behind the striker” rather than on the left, where he operated without reward at the World Cup, or in the variety of roles that Slot tried without success.Wirtz supplying Isak and/or Hugo Ekitiké was always the intended plan of attack for Liverpool last season. The trio ultimately played only 119 minutes together as injuries struck. That stat was never lost on Slot as hewas ushered to the exitafter a turbulent and toxic campaign.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionLiverpool need a very good version of Isak, too. The excuse of playing catch-up having missed pre-season, or almost four months of the season due to a fractured ankle and fibula, no longer washes for a striker who featured in all four games of Sweden’s World Cup. Isak has looked sharp in pre-season training. He not only has to sustain that sharpness next season but convince he is a suitable fit for this Liverpool team.View image in fullscreenFlorian Wirtz will be used behind the striker this season under Andoni Iraola for Liverpool.Photograph: Becky Oliver/LFC/Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesIraola’s options and vision for Liverpool will improve as senior names return but he undoubtedly requires more help through the transfer market. Work is under way ona move for Bradley Barcola, who is open to leaving Paris Saint-Germain for Anfield, but a deal for a winger who the European champions value at £145m is yet to be struck.A lack of defensive cover cost Liverpool last season and remains a glaring issue, and there are doubts over the futures of Curtis Jones, Federico Chiesa and Harvey Elliott, among others.Liverpool’s head coach has admitted he “hates this month of August” because of the uncertainty that surrounds players while the season starts. “It’s difficult to build a proper team with a lot of question marks,” he added. Between Soldier Field on Sunday and St James’ Park on 23 August, the building work must accelerate.Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolAndoni IraolaLeeds UnitedChicago FirefeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Yealimi Noh leads Women’s Open by three shots after Ryu Hae-ran stumbles | Women's Open | The Guardian
description: Ryu’s bid for a third consecutive major win is in doubt, while England’s Lottie Woad and Charley Hull remain in contention at Royal Lytham and St Annes
Author: Ewan Murray
Headline: Ryu’s bid for a third consecutive major win is in doubt, while England’s Lottie Woad and Charley Hull remain in contention at Royal Lytham and St Annes
Content: Yealimi Noh leads Ryu Hae-ran, Jeeno Thitikul, Lucy Li, Esther Henseleit and Shiho Kuwaki by four shots on seven under par.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAView image in fullscreenYealimi Noh leads Ryu Hae-ran, Jeeno Thitikul, Lucy Li, Esther Henseleit and Shiho Kuwaki by four shots on seven under par.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAWomen's OpenYealimi Noh leads Women’s Open by three shots after Ryu Hae-ran stumblesRyu’s bid for third consecutive major win in doubtEngland’s Lottie Woad and Charley Hull in contentionEwan Murrayat Royal Lytham & St AnnesSat 1 Aug 2026 14.38 EDTLast modified on Sat 1 Aug 2026 15.18 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRyu Hae-ran has 18 holes to recover from events in the third round of the Women’s Open. Her stumble at Royal Lytham and St Annes would have counted as one of the most remarkable in recent major championship memory had it taken place a day later. Saturday proved it is never, ever over on terrain such as this. Adam Scott can verify that, such was his horrible capitulation here as Ernie Els claimed the Open of 2012. There must be something about Lytham.Ryu is looking to set an extraordinary record of three major wins in as many starts. Early in the third round, she looked firmly on course for that. The South Korean marched to a four-shot lead after four. Her advantage was the same on the 7th tee. By the time she walked from the 18th green, Ryu was three adrift of Yealimi Noh. Quite the turnaround. How damaging? That remains to be seen.Charley Hull doubles down on caddie prank after strong start to Women’s OpenRead moreRyu joined Jeeno Thitikul, Lucy Li, Esther Henseleit and Shiho Kuwaki on an aggregate of four under par. That group is the closest to Noh.Lytham provides a fiendishly difficult test. Ryu looked unflappable until the 7th, where she cracked a drive right, towards the railway line between Blackpool South and Preston. After a penalty drop, a bogey hardly seemed disastrous. Yet it triggered a horrible run. Ryu made bogey on the 8th, 10th, 12th and 14th after finding a series of bunkers. Her lead, one at the turn, had evaporated by the 10th when she found herself level with Kuwaki.As Ryu was faltering, Noh delivered a links masterclass. Her 69 included an inward half of 33. Noh’s prominence here is a surprise, given her overall major record is not particularly impressive. “It was a little bit of a rocky start,” said Noh, who was three over through six. “But my putting was solid after that and my shots too. I just settled into a better routine and focused on my tempo on the back nine.“It’s just another round of golf out there tomorrow and I’m going to enjoy it. I’m just happy to be in this position and ready to go again.”Nelly Korda birdied the 17th to move to one under par. The world No 1 could have been considered in the mix at that point but a horrible double bogey at the last followed, which surely ended her Women’s Open dream. The eight-shot gap is not the only problem for Korda, instead the number of strong players between her and Noh. Lydia Ko is one of them and feels notable at minus one.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Home hope remains alive. Lottie Woad’s 70 means she is very much in touch at three under.Charley Hull is just a stroke further backafter her 71. Hull claimed she played like a 10-handicap amateur in the early stages of her round. The vagaries of Lytham mean any player within sight of the lead going into the final day has a legitimate hope of glory. Woad’s unflustered nature is an advantage here while Hull is long overdue major success.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“The more times you’re in that position the more comfortable you get,” said Woad. “I know I can play well in this tournament and I have done the last two years and had that experience of being in the mix. And even this year, obviously a few weeks ago I was leading at the Evian Championship, so I can kind of use that experience as well. The more times you put the yourself in that position is obviously a good thing.“It’s always great when the fans are pulling for you. I mean, it’s not all going to be on me tomorrow. Charley is playing great too, so people going to be supporting both of us.” Indeed they are. As Ryu already knows, she is firmly up against it in her bid to make history.Explore more on these topicsWomen's OpenGolfnewsShareReuse this content

title: Wiebes outsprints Le Court and Vollering to win Tour de France Femmes opening stage | Tour de France Femmes | The Guardian
description: Lorena Wiebes took the first yellow jersey of the 2026 Tour de France Femmes after outsprinting the race favourites Kim Le Court and Demi Vollering
Author: Jeremy Whittle
Headline: Lorena Wiebes took the first yellow jersey of the 2026 Tour de France Femmes after outsprinting the race favourites Kim Le Court and Demi Vollering
Content: Lorena Wiebes enjoys her win on the first stage of the Tour de France Femmes in Lausanne.Photograph: Denis Balibouse/ReutersView image in fullscreenLorena Wiebes enjoys her win on the first stage of the Tour de France Femmes in Lausanne.Photograph: Denis Balibouse/ReutersTour de France FemmesWiebes outsprints Le Court and Vollering to win Tour de France Femmes opening stageWiebes’ turn of speed too much for 2023 winner Vollering‘It was a long sprint, but I’m super happy’Jeremy Whittlein LausanneSat 1 Aug 2026 13.05 EDTLast modified on Sat 1 Aug 2026 16.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLorena Wiebes took the first yellow jersey of the 2026Tour de France Femmesafter climbing the Côte Saint-François and outsprinting race favourites Kim Le Court and 2023 champion, Demi Vollering.“The team worked super hard today,” Wiebes said. “When Demi attacked, I knew I had to follow. It was a long sprint, but I’m super happy.”Tour de France Femmes 2026: Lorena Wiebes powers to stage one win in Lausanne – liveRead moreIt was the Dutch rider’s sixth stage win in the Tour de France Femmes. The 27-year-old also won the opening stage of the 2026 women’s Giro d’Italia in May but was disqualified because her bike had an illegal weight, an outcome which left her team considering legal action against cycling’s governing body, the UCI.“I’m really happy with the support I have had from the team and the staff,” she said. “They fully believed in me, when even I had some doubts.”Wiebes, of SD Worx-Protime, leads the race overall by four seconds from Le Court and six seconds from Vollering. The defending champion, Pauline Ferrand-Prévot, finished eighth and is 10 seconds behind the race leader.The final outcome of the race is likely to be decided by minutes, although Lars Boom, sports director to Vollering, who lost the 2024 race by just four seconds, valued the time gain.“That’s always nice,” Boom said. “You never know what’s going to happen with wildfires in France, so in the end it’s always better to get seconds than to have to gain seconds.”The high temperatures and rolling roads split the field after 83km, on the third category Côte de Villars-le-Comte, where numerous riders lost contact with the peloton and one of the day’s four breakaways, French rider Océane Mahé of the lowly Ma Petite Entreprise team, took the lead in the Queen of the Mountains classification.But with 50km left to race the quartet’s advantage began to dwindle and they were finally swallowed up with 6km remaining, on the lakeside approach to Lausanne’s uphill finish.View image in fullscreenLorena Wiebes wears the yellow jersey on the podium.Photograph: Denis Balibouse/ReutersVollering, buoyed by the announcement that Red Bull has become her FDJ United–Suezteam’s latest sponsorship partner, led into the final 600m, but Wiebes’ turn of speed was too much for her compatriot, who was surprisingly overtaken by Le Court in the closing metres.Wiebes came to the Tour Femmes looking for vindication after the Giro controversy in late May. Her win was wiped out by disqualification after her bike weighed in at slightly under the regulation 6.8kg. Wiebes also lost the pink race leader’s jersey and a bitter dispute ensued between the team and the UCI over the methods used to measure the bike’s weight.“I would have been perfectly fine with it if the scale had consistently shown the same weight,” Wiebes said. “But having the bike’s weight vary during the weighing process – that was the most frustrating part for me.”Her SD Worx-Protime team manager, Danny Stam, said that a legal case against the UCI was now pending.“Our team’s lawyers are working on it,” he told De Telegraaf. “We’ve received feedback but it’s going to be a long process. Still, justice needs to be served.“I just find it unacceptable that a decision with such a huge impact on a rider is made when a bike is hanging from a tent that’s nearly blowing away. Can’t we operate a bit more professionally in this day and age? Can’t we just weigh a bike inside an enclosed truck, away from the wind? Instead of: ‘Now it weighs this, now it weighs that.’”Tomorrow’s second stage begins in nearby Aigle, ironically on the doorstep of the UCI headquarters, where Wiebes will take to the start line in the yellow jersey. Five more climbs and high temperatures may make it another tough stage, but the flat finish on Geneva’s Quai du Mont-Blanc looks well-suited to the Dutch rider.Explore more on these topicsTour de France FemmesCyclingUCI (Union Cycliste Internationale)newsShareReuse this content

title: Transfer news: Welbeck joins Chelsea, Brentford complete record Sangaré deal | Transfer window | The Guardian
description: Chelsea signed Brighton’s veteran striker Danny Welbeck in a deal worth a reported £5m
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Chelsea signed Brighton’s veteran striker Danny Welbeck in a deal worth a reported £5m
Content: Danny Welbeck, 35, has signed a two-year deal at Chelsea.Photograph: Chris Lee/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenDanny Welbeck, 35, has signed a two-year deal at Chelsea.Photograph: Chris Lee/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesTransfer windowTransfer news: Welbeck joins Chelsea, Brentford complete record Sangaré deal35-year-old Brighton striker Welbeck seals £5m moveMali international Sangaré joins Bees for reported £39mAgenciesSat 1 Aug 2026 12.44 EDTLast modified on Sat 1 Aug 2026 12.59 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleChelsea have signed Brighton’s veteran striker Danny Welbeck in a deal worth a reported £5m. Welbeck has agreed a two-year contract and will link up with Xabi Alonso’s squad on their pre-season tour.The 35-year-old’s move to Stamford Bridge is a break from Chelsea’s policy of signing younger players with the potential to be developed. It is the first time they have paid a transfer fee for a player over the age of 26 since they signed Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang from Barcelona in 2022 when the striker was 33.Chelsea fined £10m and given suspended transfer ban by FA over agent breachesRead more“When you hear of interest from Chelsea, it’s something that fills you with such immense pride. Knowing the history of Chelsea, it’s a club that wants to win trophies and is pushing to do that every single season,” Welbeck said.“I’m really honoured to come to a club of this stature at what feels like a really exciting time. I know a few of the boys already and I’ve had fantastic conversations with the manager and already feel that connection. I’ve got that fire in my belly and I’m ready to give it everything for this club to make everyone at Chelsea, and the supporters, proud.”Alonso was keen to add experience to his squad after last season’s disappointing 10th-place finish in the Premier League. He opted for Welbeck after the former Manchester United and Arsenal forward enjoyed a memorable campaign with Brighton.Welbeck, who has 42 caps for England, scored 13 goals in 37 Premier League games last term after netting 10 times in 2024-25.Welbeck’s arrival in west London will raise questions about the future of Chelsea striker Liam Delap, who signed from Ipswich last season, as well as fellow forwards Nicolas Jackson and Marc Guiu.Welbeck is the latest player to move from Brighton to Chelsea in recent years after João Pedro, Moisés Caicedo, Robert Sánchez and Marc Cucurella, whojoined Real Madridearlier this summer.Chelsea spent a British record £117m to sign the England forward Morgan Rogers, 24, from Aston Villa in July. They also securedthe France defender Maxence Lacroix, 26, from Crystal Palace for £52m earlier this week and signed Atalanta defender Marco Palestra, 21, for £43m.Brentford seal record Sangaré dealBrentfordhave signed the Mali international Mamadou Sangaré from ⁠Lens for a club-record fee, reported to be £39m. Sangaré, 24, joinsBrentfordon a five-year contract, with ⁠the option to extend for another year.“Mamadou ​is someone ‌that we’ve tracked ‌for quite some time. He’s been on ‌our radar and was a player we were really keen to bring in,” the Brentford head coach Keith Andrews said. “He’s a humble young man, but he’s equally as ⁠determined to succeed in his career. He ​fits ​everything we want from ​a Brentford player, on and ​off the ‌pitch.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSangaré left Austria’s Rapid Vienna to ‌joinLenslast year, and featured prominently as they won the ​French Cup for the first time and finished second in Ligue 1.View image in fullscreenMamadou Sangaré has swapped RC Lens for Brentford in a £39m move.Photograph: Stéphanie Lecocq/ReutersBournemouthhave announced the signing of António Silva from Benfica for a fee believed to be in the region of £25m. The 22-year-old defender becomes new manager Marco Rose’s second signing of the summer after the arrival of Álvaro Rodríguez earlier this week.Silva made 235 senior appearances forBenficaand collected six major honours during his time in Portugal. He told the club website: “I am very happy to be here. It’s a pleasure to play for Bournemouth and in the Premier League.“The mentality is always to win. I will try my best, and I will play for the fans. We have everything here that helps us perform on the pitch, and I can’t wait to get started.”Explore more on these topicsTransfer windowChelseaBrighton & Hove AlbionBrentfordLensBournemouthBenficanewsShareReuse this content

title: De Zerbi wants ‘lovely guy’ Richarlison to stay at Tottenham after winner sinks Chelsea | Roberto De Zerbi | The Guardian
description: Tottenham beat Chelsea 2-1 in a friendly in Sydney despite Kevin Danso being sent off, as Roberto De Zerbi backed Richarlison to stay at the club and be a success
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Tottenham beat Chelsea 2-1 in a friendly in Sydney despite Kevin Danso being sent off, as Roberto De Zerbi backed Richarlison to stay at the club and be a success
Content: Richarlison scored a stoppage-time winner for Tottenham against Chelsea in Sydney.Photograph: Ayush Kumar/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenRicharlison scored a stoppage-time winner for Tottenham against Chelsea in Sydney.Photograph: Ayush Kumar/Getty ImagesRoberto De ZerbiDe Zerbi wants ‘lovely guy’ Richarlison to stay at Tottenham after winner sinks Chelsea10-man Spurs win pre-season match 2-1 in Sydney‘He’s important, it’s not easy to find another striker’Adam Hancock at the Accor StadiumSat 1 Aug 2026 11.02 EDTLast modified on Sat 1 Aug 2026 11.29 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRoberto De Zerbi wants Richarlison to stay at Tottenham, but says the striker, who has been linked with a move away, is still unsure about his future.The Brazilian scored a last-gasp winner as 10-man Tottenham defeatedChelsea2-1 in a pre-season friendly in Sydney, with Kevin Danso sent off just minutes after coming on as a half-time substitute.Arsenal’s title defence: keeping tired players fit and the Vinícius questionRead moreSpeaking after the game, De Zerbi said Richarlison had not clarified if he was going to depart this summer. “I don’t know, I didn’t understand well, because sometimes he said to stay, sometimes he leaves, we have to speak. Anyway, there is not any problem, he’s a lovely guy. All of us love him, the teammates, the club, the staff, because he works hard every day.”Richarlison has less than a year left on his contract after joining Tottenham from Everton in 2022. He has struggled to find consistent form during his time in north London but De Zerbi said it would be difficult to replace his goals.“For me he’s still an important player because it’s not so easy to find another striker as Richarlison, because Richarlison scored goals and he knows the way. The new striker, we don’t know, the other striker, we don’t know. He [Richarlison] scored 12 goals last season, not for luck, because he feels the way to score.”Richarlison bagged a 92nd-minute winner for Tottenham against Chelsea in front of more than 80,000 fans at Sydney’s Accor Stadium. The Brazilian was the first player to react after Jamie Donley’s shot came back off a post, prodding the ball into an empty net to avert the need for a penalty shootout.It was the first time that the two sides have met outside the UK and the match started in the spirit of a true London derby. Conor Gallagher flew into a challenge on Dário Essugo after 10 minutes, picking up a yellow card and a fair few heckles from the largely Chelsea-supporting crowd. Jan Paul van Hecke clattered into João Pedro, while Dominic Solanke and Levi Colwill tussled off the ball.This fixture has had its fair share of red cards over the years and there was another one to add to the list, after Danso was sent off three minutes after coming off the bench. A poor surface got the better of the Spurs defender as he failed to control a backpass, allowing João Pedro to run on to the ball and through on goal. Danso lunged headfirst into the Chelsea forward, with the referee reaching straight for his pocket.View image in fullscreenKevin Danso is shown a red card three minutes after coming on as a substitute.Photograph: David Neilson/EPADe Zerbi said the sending off made the game harder for both sides. “It was worse for us and for Chelsea, because if you consider the condition of the pitch, very bad. And if you consider we are starting from two weeks, maybe less than three weeks, the second half you start the fatigue and playing, attacking against 10 players behind the line of the ball is tough for every team.”De Zerbi’s side were on top in the early stages and took a deserved lead on 17 minutes when the new signing Sandro Tonali scored his first goal for Tottenham. The midfielder’s side-footed effort from outside the area took a deflection, wrong-footing the Chelsea goalkeeper Teddy Sharman-Lowe before nestling into the bottom corner.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSpurs were only ahead for four minutes, as Estêvão Willian got the better of Andy Robertson to head home at the back post after some good work from Jamie Gittens down the left.The game lost its competitive edge in the second half with both sides making a flurry of substitutions, before Richarlison settled it at the death.Chelsea will now head to Hong Kong where they will be joined by Mykhailo Mudryk, who has been cleared to play again after the Football Association and the World Anti-Doping Agency resolved his appeal against a ban for failing a doping test. The Ukrainian winger was suspended for four years after failing a drug test in 2024. De Zerbi, who managed Mudryk at Shakhtar Donetsk, said he viewed the player as one of his “sons”.“I’m very happy – he deserves to play, he’s a good guy, top player. Hopefully he can show what he suffered in the last two years, in the next season, maybe not against Tottenham, but he’s a lovely guy and he’s a very, very good player.”Explore more on these topicsRoberto De ZerbiFriendliesChelseaTottenham HotspurnewsShareReuse this content

title: Scottish Premiership: Mayo and Nisbet strike late to help Aberdeen stun Hearts | Scottish Premiership | The Guardian
description: Stoppage-time goals secured Aberdeen a 2-1 win against Hearts, while Killian Phillips’ double gave St Mirren a 2-0 win at Falkirk in the Scottish Premiership
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Stoppage-time goals secured Aberdeen a 2-1 win against Hearts, while Killian Phillips’ double gave St Mirren a 2-0 win at Falkirk in the Scottish Premiership
Content: Kevin Nisbet plays to the crowd after scoring Aberdeen’s 95th-minute winner.Photograph: Mark Scates/SNS GroupView image in fullscreenKevin Nisbet plays to the crowd after scoring Aberdeen’s 95th-minute winner.Photograph: Mark Scates/SNS GroupScottish PremiershipScottish Premiership: Mayo and Nisbet strike late to help Aberdeen stun HeartsTwo stoppage-time goals secured 2-1 win for the hostsKillian Phillips double gives St Mirren 2-0 win at FalkirkPA MediaSat 1 Aug 2026 15.21 EDTLast modified on Sat 1 Aug 2026 16.48 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHearts’ miserable summer continued as they conceded two late goals to lose 2-1 toAberdeenin their Premiership opener at Pittodrie.Wouter Vrancken andHeartslooked on course for a much-needed victory after a turbulent few months as they led through Oisin McEntee’s first-half goal. But just as they looked to be closing out a first win at Pittodrie for more than a decade, Lewis Mayo equalised in the 90th minute before Kevin Nisbet won it for Aberdeen with a stoppage-time penalty after Stuart Findlay was sent off for denying a goal-scoring opportunity.Rangers held by Dundee United to kick off McInnes era and Scottish PremiershipRead moreIt was a third consecutive defeat for Vrancken, who has endured a chastening start since replacing Derek McInnes in June.The Aberdeen manager, Stephen Robinson, whose side had built up some momentum by winning each of their four Premier Sports Cup group-stage matches, pitched Chris Cadden straight into his starting lineup a day after he joined from Hibernian.There were five changes to the Hearts side that lost Wednesday’s Champions League qualifier at home to Sturm Graz, with the goalkeeper Beau Reus and Laurent Mendy handed their debuts and Sabah Kerjota – more than a year after joining – and Amadou Ba-Sy given their first competitive starts.In what was their first league match since beingpipped to the title by Celticin May, the 1,600-strong travelling support could be regularly heard singing anti-Scottish Football Association songs in protest at the contentious calls from officials in the closing matches of last season that they felt cost them dear in their quest for glory.Following a summer of transition and a 6-0 aggregate defeat by Sturm Graz that had done little to improve the mood of the fans since that agonising end to the past campaign, there was a sense of trepidation in some quarters about the prospect of kicking off the new season at Pittodrie, where they had not won in their previous 14 visits.Hearts’ makeshift defence – with the midfielder McEntee playing at centre-half following an injury to Malachi Fagan-Walcott – looked to have allowed the Aberdeen captain Nisbet to get clean through in the third minute but McEntee recovered well to scramble the ball behind for a corner.Nisbet then glanced a header just wide from Connor Ronan’s corner in the 27th minute, although clear chances were generally at a premium.Hearts made the breakthrough in the 35th minute after some pinball in the penalty area. Ba-Sy’s cutback from the left broke to Blair Spittal, whose shot was blocked by Nesta Guinness-Walker on the edge of the six-yard box and the fellow defender Dan Happe’s attempt to clear ran into the path of McEntee, who shot low into the net from seven yards.The visitors generally looked comfortable for most of the second period, with Cláudio Braga spurning a good chance to double their lead.Aberdeen had offered little as an attacking force but they levelled in the 90th minute when Mayo bundled in from close range after Happe headed Ronan’s free-kick back into the danger area.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe dramatic turnaround was completed in stoppage time when Toyosi Olusanya was hauled down by Findlay, who saw red, and Nisbet despatched the spot-kick.TheSt Mirrenmanager, Craig McLeish, believes his team’s 2-0 win atFalkirkaugurs well for a successful campaign.McLeish is convinced his squad will improve on last season’s struggles before he steered Saints to safety when the interim head coach.He has set a high bar of the top six and a European qualification bid this term, and a double from Killian Phillips helped St Mirren get off to a fine start atFalkirkStadium.“I thought the performance was excellent and if we can build on that we can go and achieve something as a group,” McLeish said. “I’m delighted for the group. We got the result our performance deserved. I thought we were excellent.”Explore more on these topicsScottish PremiershipAberdeenHeartsSt MirrenFalkirkShareReuse this content

title: Amanda Staveley consortium set to buy Gold family’s 25.1% stake in West Ham | West Ham United | The Guardian
description: A consortium led by Amanda Staveley has reached an agreement to buy a ‌25.1% stake in West ⁠Ham after Vanessa Gold ⁠agreed to sell ⁠her ​family’s shares in the Championship club
Author: Andy Martin
Headline: A consortium led by Amanda Staveley has reached an agreement to buy a ‌25.1% stake in West ⁠Ham after Vanessa Gold ⁠agreed to sell ⁠her ​family’s shares in the Championship club
Content: Former Newcastle  director Amanda Staveley has made her move for a stake in West Ham.Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenFormer Newcastle  director Amanda Staveley has made her move for a stake in West Ham.Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/ReutersWest Ham UnitedAmanda Staveley consortium set to buy Gold family’s 25.1% stake in West HamPreviously agreed sale to Daniel Kretinsky falls throughVanessa Gold, daughter of former chair, is selling ⁠upAndy MartinSat 1 Aug 2026 11.50 EDTLast modified on Sat 1 Aug 2026 12.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA consortium led by Amanda Staveley has reached an agreement to buy a ‌25.1% stake in West ⁠Ham after Vanessa Gold, daughter of the former chair David Gold, ⁠agreed to sell ⁠her ​family’s shares in theChampionshipclub.The move by the businesswoman who helped lead the Saudi consortium takeover of Newcastle comes after a previously agreed sale to fellow shareholder and Czech businessman ⁠Daniel Kretinsky fell through.Have you ever switched allegiance as a football fan? You are not alone | Luke McLaughlinRead moreThe Gold family ​trust owns the 25.1% stake in West Ham, ‌who wererelegated from the Premier Leaguelast season just two seasons afterwinning the Europa Conference Leaguein 2023. However, current shareholders will also be presented with the chance to buy out the Gold family under an ongoing process.Gold said in a statement: “As the daughter of David Gold, it was a great honour to step into a joint chair and director role at the club following his passing in 2023. Whether as a youth team player, a lifelong fan or an owner, my father’s priority was always to champion and protect this great club. Over the past three years I have taken huge personal pride in continuing that legacy and will always be hugely grateful to the staff, players and fans who allowed me to do so.“On June 12, Daniel Kretínsky and I agreed a sale that would have made EP Group the single largest shareholder in West Ham. Unfortunately, since that time, the original deal and other alternatives that we have discussed could not be brought to fruition.View image in fullscreenWest Ham were relegated from the Premier League last season.Photograph: Eddie Keogh/Reuters“In light of this, I have now reached an agreement to sell my family’s shareholding to a consortium led by Amanda Staveley, Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners. This sale remains subject to a pre-emption process, under which existing shareholders have the option to buy the shares instead.“While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions. My ambition throughout this process has been to ensure the club has the right leadership and ownership to enable West Ham to achieve its potential and return to its rightful place in the Premier League.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“Amanda Staveley, Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners will bring deep experience and understanding of what it takes to lead a successful football club, and I have every confidence in what she and her partners can bring to West Ham. While the sale process proceeds, I will continue to act in the club’s best interests, as my father did and would expect of me.”Staveley brokered the deal which allowed a Saudi-backed consortium to buy-out then Newcastle owner Mike Ashley in October 2021, and she and Ghodoussi oversaw the club’s rise from Premier League relegation candidates to Champions League participants and, after their departure during the summer of 2024, Carabao Cup winners.The Hammers dropped out of the top flight at the end of last season and will begin the process of attempting to secure a swift return at Burnley on 16 August.Explore more on these topicsWest Ham UnitedChampionshipnewsShareReuse this content

title: Marketing stunt or ‘extraordinary’ transfer? Ravenna fans ride wave of the Ronaldinho Effect | Ronaldinho | The Guardian
description: Brazil legend’s decision to play in Serie C at the age of 46 has divided fans – but the man who arranged the deal has high hopes
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Brazil legend’s decision to play in Serie C at the age of 46 has divided fans – but the man who arranged the deal has high hopes
Content: (From left) Ravenna fans Francesco Zannoni, Fabio Pagani, Giovanni Lama and Marcello Lama are looking forward to watching Ronaldinho.Photograph: Roberto Salomone/The GuardianView image in fullscreen(From left) Ravenna fans Francesco Zannoni, Fabio Pagani, Giovanni Lama and Marcello Lama are looking forward to watching Ronaldinho.Photograph: Roberto Salomone/The GuardianRonaldinhoMarketing stunt or ‘extraordinary’ transfer? Ravenna fans ride wave of the Ronaldinho EffectBrazil legend’s decision to play in Serie C at 46 has divided fans – but the man who arranged the deal has high hopesEmanuele Giulianelli in RavennaSat 1 Aug 2026 03.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOn a scorching summer afternoon in Ravenna, a city far better known for its fifth-century Byzantine mosaics and Dante’s tomb than for footballing glory, eyes are peeled in the historic centre for one of world football’s most recognisable figures – a man who featured in the World Cup final half-time show alongside Madonna and Ronaldo: Ronaldo de Assis Moreira, better known asRonaldinho.“We haven’t seen him yet,” four Ravenna supporters sitting at a cafe say with dry irony as they flip through La Gazzetta dello Sport, Italy’s famous pink sports daily. They are undeniably sceptical,viewing the signingas a purely commercial operation, yet deep down they still harbour the dream of seeing the 2005 Ballon d’Or and 2002 World Cup winner wear their yellow and red shirt.‘Let the magic begin’: Ronaldinho signs for Serie C side Ravenna at age of 46Read moreIt is a small, surreal glimpse into the whirlwind that has engulfed this quiet corner of Emilia-Romagna, thanks to the business instinct of Ignazio Cipriani. Heir to the Venetian hospitality dynasty behind the renowned Harry’s Bar, Cipriani took over the club in 2024 when they were in Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football. A native of Ravenna, he is the grandson of Raul Gardini, the Italian chemicals tycoon and sailor who steered Il Moro di Venezia to the 1992 America’s Cup final.In his first year as president, Cipriani oversaw victory in the Serie D Cup and promotion to the professional ranks of Serie C. But that is merely the first step in a long ascent, he says: “It’s not a provocation. Serie A is the goal I declared from day one because I intend to reach it. And the Champions League remains the ultimate horizon we want to walk towards, step by step. I made this statement because I like working with my back against the wall: when you have no way out, you are forced to find solutions instead of excuses. I prefer to remove every alibi from the beginning.”And this summer, Cipriani pulled off a surprise move – so surprising that anyone reading the headlines assumed it was a prank: bringing the 46-year-old Ronaldinho back as a player.View image in fullscreenRonaldinho holds up a Ravenna top with Ignazio Cipriani, the club president, after the surprise move was announced in Miami in June.Photograph: Rebecca Blackwell/AP“We met through Lorenzo Tonetti and Ariedo Braida,” Cipriani says, “two people who worked for over 20 years at AC Milan and had Ronaldinho as a player. The idea of involving him was a dream I cultivated as soon as I bought the club. Thanks to Lorenzo and Ariedo, we met, started talking, and a genuine friendship grew. From that relationship came many ideas for the club’s growth. And to the question everyone is asking, I am happy to answer: Ronaldinho will wear the Ravenna shirt as a player, and he will try – maybe scoring the last goal of his career with us!”Meanwhile, a dedicated website has already put a special-edition shirt on sale featuring the “R10” logo – the Brazilian’s personal brand – which sold out within a few hours. It represents a striking collision of high-end global branding, small-town football, and brilliantly executed marketing stunt.“If someone had told me three years ago that Ronaldinho was coming to Ravenna, I would have sent them straight to the psychiatric ward,” says Fabio laughing, a lifelong supporter. “The night the news broke, international headlines everywhere read ‘Ronaldinho to Ravenna’. It was an extraordinary operation.”Ravenna is no footballing giant. Plagued by bankruptcies in 2001 and 2012, the club has spent decades bouncing around the lower tiers, with seven seasons in Serie B the highest point. Historically a volleyball stronghold, the football scene was accustomed to modest budgets and regional rivalries.View image in fullscreenRonaldinho will be aiming to wow the crowds at Ravenna’s Stadio Bruno Benelli this season.Photograph: Roberto Salomone/The Guardian“Ronaldinho is a unique icon,” Cipriani says. “His way of playing made my generation fall in love with the game. We want him today to make the next generation of fans, in Italy and around the world, fall in love with Ravenna . It’s not just a visibility stunt; it’s about building a bridge between different eras of football and growing a truly global fanbase around it.”To support this ambitious sporting and industrial project, the club is working with the municipality to renovate the Stadio Bruno Benelli, increasing its capacity beyond 6,300. But the president’s ultimate dream is a new multi-purpose venue open seven days a week, featuring retail spaces, concert facilities, and an integrated Hotel Cipriani linked to the city’s international tourism expansion.For Ravenna’s mayor, Alessandro Barattoni, the arrival of a world-famous figure fits neatly into a broader strategy to promote the city globally. In recent years, Ravenna has been expanding its international reach beyond traditional beach tourism and commercial ports. The city is enjoying renewed ties with the Anglo-Saxon world, highlighted by a recent visit from the British royal family and the opening of the Lord Byron Museum.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“Ronaldinho brings a whole new level of global fame,” Barattoni says. “When the news broke, my phone exploded with messages from former schoolmates. For younger kids today, he might be someone to discover on YouTube, but the fascination remains intact.” With a smile, the mayor adds that, schedule permitting, he would be delighted to personally guide Ronaldinho on a tour of the city’s cultural heritage.However, Barattoni is quick to clarify the institution’s role: “Our common ground with the club is internationalisation: bringing Ravenna’s image to the world. Ronaldinho has been a global ambassador for countless brands. There is an overarching project that can bring great visibility to the team and allow the city to showcase its initiatives beyond standard routes.” He adds: “Even before Ronaldinho’s arrival, the club did a fantastic job engaging younger generations. The average age in the stands is lower, more vibrant, and more engaged than ever before. A genuine sense of community is forming.”View image in fullscreenAlessandro Barattoni, the mayor of Ravenna, is confident the Ronaldinho transfer will be positive for the Italian city.Photograph: Roberto Salomone/The GuardianYet, fears of a hyper-commercialised image linger among traditional supporters. In the Curva Mero, such marketing moves are approached with caution. “There is a certain reluctance among some factions,” Fabio admits. “Modern football pushes values that many don’t share: rising ticket prices, losing accessibility for lower-income families. As a result, visibility and marketing stunts risk being viewed sideways.”Cipriani demonstrates an acute awareness of these dynamics: “Without roots, no global project makes sense,” the president says. “Ravenna is not a brand we are building from scratch; it’s a history and an identity that existed before us. Tradition isn’t a brake on ambition: it’s the foundation. A club without its people is worth nothing.”“I’m 50 years old and I’ve been coming to the stadium since my school days,” says Giovanni, another fan. “I’m rediscovering the enthusiasm of the past. If it takes an icon like Ronaldinho and a local entrepreneur to make us dream of Serie A, then so be it. The important thing is never to forget the people in the stands.”Riding the wave of the “Ronaldinho Effect”, the season-ticket campaign has just launched with a target of selling 2,800. Ticket prices have risen by an average of about 12%, with variations across different stadium sections.For now, Ravenna is soaking up a dizzying, galvanising atmosphere. On the pitch, the club is assembling a squad to win the league; off it, the city awaits 20 August, when Ronaldinho is expected to appear during a three-day summer festival in nearby Marina di Ravenna, organised in signature Cipriani style.Explore more on these topicsRonaldinhofeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Podium sweep and relay gold cap Australia’s record athletics haul at Commonwealth Games | Commonwealth Games 2026 | The Guardian
description: Australia delivered an unprecedented podium sweep in the women’s mile on the final day of athletics competition at the Commonwealth Games
Author: Jack Snape
Headline: Australia delivered an unprecedented podium sweep in the women’s mile on the final day of athletics competition at the Commonwealth Games
Content: Jessica Hull (silver), Abbey Caldwell (gold) and Claudia Hollingsworth (bronze) of celebrate a clean sweep in the women's mile.Photograph: Joel Carrett/AAPView image in fullscreenJessica Hull (silver), Abbey Caldwell (gold) and Claudia Hollingsworth (bronze) of celebrate a clean sweep in the women's mile.Photograph: Joel Carrett/AAPCommonwealth Games 2026Podium sweep and relay gold cap Australia’s record athletics haul at Commonwealth GamesOne-two-three for Caldwell, Hull and Hollingsworth in women’s mileMen’s 4x100m relay team claim one of seven golds won on day nineJack SnapeSat 1 Aug 2026 19.02 EDTLast modified on Sat 1 Aug 2026 19.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAustralia delivered an unprecedented podium sweep in the women’s mile on the final day of athletics competition at theCommonwealth Games, after Abbey Caldwell upset Jessica Hull to secure one of seven track and field gold medals including a breakthrough victory for Lachie Kennedy’s 4x100m relay team.The haul exceeds the six gold medals from one day in Auckland in 1950, when Marjorie Jackson and Shirley Strickland were among the winners, to make it Australia’s most successful track and field day at the Commonwealth Games.Josh Kerr storms to Commonwealth Games mile title in golden Glasgow momentRead moreCaldwell held off Hull and a fast-finishing Claudia Hollingsworth in the final race of the evening. “It is a privilege to line up with people like Jess and Clauds,” Caldwell told Channel Seven after securing Australia’s first gold medal in the women’s mile at the Commonwealth Games. “Getting onto the track, they are my main competitors, and for them to be from the same nation is unbelievable, so watch out for us Aussie girls in the coming years.”Hull’s silver is her second of the Games, after she finished behind another Australian, Rose Davies, in the 5000m. “I heard them [the stadium commentators] say with about 40 to go, that the Australians are going to sweep, and I was just like, ‘Oh my god!’,” she said.The win in the men’s relay was Australia’s first in the event for 52 years, secured after the team trusted each other with faster but riskier baton hand-offs. “We all knew we were capable of getting gold today, so all our [handover] marks, we pushed them out [stretched them], and we just sent it,” Kennedy said. “We gave it everything we had and I mean, credit to everyone here, and shout out Chris [Ius] for running the heat this morning.”View image in fullscreenRohan Browning, Calab Law, Josh Azzopardi and Lachie Kennedy celebrate.Photograph: Ian MacNicol/Getty ImagesKennedy handed the baton to Josh Azzopardi, who had complained before the Games about Rowan Browning being preferred to him for selection in individual 100m. Azzopardi maintained the lead and passed onto Kennedy’s training partner Calab Law, who handed Browning just enough of a buffer to hold off the Olympic champions Canada.Browning glanced to his inside on the line to see for himself the margin of four hundredths of a second. “I don’t think I’ve ever run quite that scared in my life,” said the veteran, who shared an embrace with Azzopardi at the line.“Four years ago, I tripped over, got the team DQd [disqualified] in the heat, when I think we were medal threats, and I’ve had to carry the burden of that for the past four years,” Browning said. “This hopefully wipes the slate clean, and it’s probably the most special moment of my career.”Mackenzie Little claimed victory in the javelin, adding to Australian wins in the morning session by Matt Denny in discus and Rhiannon Clarke in the T38 200m. The day began with another Australian one-two-three, when Jemima Montag finished ahead of Elizabeth McMillen and Rebecca Henderson in the 10,000m walk.View image in fullscreenMackenzie Little launches a javelin on her way to gold.Photograph: Ben Stansall/AFP/Getty ImagesThe procession of gold was bookended by Kurtis Marschall, who won a third pole vault title in a row in the Glasgow night, clearing 5.85m to surpass by 5cm the Commonwealth Games record of Steve Hooker set in Melbourne in 2006. “It couldn’t have been more of a fairytale ending if I asked for one, mate,” Marschall said.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe 29-year-old is one of just six men in Commonwealth Games history to win three successive gold medals. He said he planned on coming back in India in 2030 to try to make it four, but for now his focus is on eclipsing Hooker’s Australian record of 6.06m.Jamaica stun Australia as England miss out on Commonwealth Games netball finalRead moreThe mark is just 6cm above Marschall’s best of 6.00m, which he has now cleared three times in 2026 already. “I really wanted that Comm Games record, Steve’s had that long enough, and he’s had the Aus record long enough, too, so, I’m coming for that,” Marschall said.Luke Boyes won silver in the 800m, as did Ky Robinson in the 5,000m to back up his 10,000m gold, and Cam Myers alsofinished a strong secondin the highly anticipated showdown over a mile with world record holder Josh Kerr.The Australian was disappointed afterwards. “That was just an awful race, I couldn’t even give him a challenge, and that’s the disappointing part,” Myers said. The 20-year-old was boxed in for much of the race and missed a brief window to go with the charging Scot with 200m left.“It’s the hesitation, when you’re on someone’s shoulder then you’ve just got to go, and if you don’t go, someone goes around you,” Myers said. “I had a perfect position with a lap to go, and I lost it to two or three guys, and I gave Kerr a fucking – sorry – a three-metre head start at 200 to go, so you can’t do that at this level. He beat me, and fair play to him.”Explore more on these topicsCommonwealth Games 2026Commonwealth GamesAthleticsAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content
